description: One port-local day of a port's own movement list: every vessel arrival and departure as the port lists it, with vessel name, IMO, MMSI and call sign as listed, status, and expected and recorded times in UTC. An arrival is placed by its recorded arrival (else the arrival the list expects), a departure by its recorded departure. What a recorded arrival means differs by port: instant_kind says whether it is the port entry or the berthing. A vessel absent from the day is not listed by the port; read_that_day false means the list was not read that day at all, so an absence says nothing. total counts every movement of the day: while next_cursor is not null, call again with the same locode and cursor set to it. A movement the port revises between pages can move across a page boundary: re-read from the first page for one consistent snapshot. Ports come from list_ports.

cursor.description: next_cursor from the previous answer, to read the next page; give the same locode with it. Omit for the first page.

date.description: Port-local day YYYY-MM-DD. Defaults to today at the port, or to the cursor's day.

limit.description: Max movements per page (1-200). Defaults to 100.

locode.description: UN/LOCODE of the port from list_ports, e.g. SEGOT; a dock code answers for its port.

name: get_port_board
title: Port arrivals and departures
